summary: Our project addresses complexity. Given that lunar landing mission timelines often differ from the original set time due to various factors. A rapid intuitive tool that allows alternative landing sites to be assessed and selected, in light of new information where mission date or landing location is changed, can assist in accelerating the process of choosing the alternative site or date. Therefore, Project Horizon Mask has been designed as an interactive web application that allows users to choose a location on the moon and enter mission date and time to learn the best possible landing site coordinates based on Sun Elevation and Earth Visibility.
details:
Horizon mask provides an interactive 3D Moon which allows users to select different sites, enter date and time to assess the landing conditions across various sites, and allows distinct locations on the Moon to be compared for decision making. It consists of terrain evaluation, mapping the mountains and slopes on the Moon's surface. Displays parameters of astronomy for understanding Sun elevation and Earth visibility. Providing temperature of the area selected, along with adopted antennas allowing users to gauge communication constraints.

It is beneficial to users in determining the best lunar landing site, incase of changes in mission timeline in light of new information, if mission dates or locations need to be alternated, this application provides a scientific prototype for turning complex space data into an interactive and understandable platform.

Tools and software used for development include JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Render and SI tool used is Chat GPT. The goal of the project was to reduce complexity for users in comparison to already existing tools, the focus was on presenting data in a clean interface with real NASA data.

Taking creativity on board in addition to our interactive web application, our team implemented a 3D map of the moon, with green points indicating best potential landing sites based on the Sun elevation and Earth visibility, displaying mountains, terrains and temperature of the particular Moon region.

Our team considered factors such as employing actual validated NASA datasets, and focused on maintaining a user-friendly application throughout.
